Angle between two curves
Rate of change

Tangent from an external point to a curve

Curves touching each other
Approximation using differentials
s.f: f(a+h)\approx f(a)+hf'(a);\qquad\text{percentage error in } y=x^n:\ n\times(\text{percentage error in } x)

s.q: Increasing and decreasing
s.n: $f'\ge0$ with equality only at isolated points still gives strictly increasing.

s.q: Using monotonicity for inequalities
Monotonic on an interval — conditions on a parameter
s.f: f'(x)\ge0\ \forall x\ \text{(with equality at isolated points)}\Rightarrow\text{use } D\le0 \text{ or min value}\ge0

Comparing numbers via monotonic functions
Standard inequalities from monotonicity
First derivative test
Second derivative test
s.n: If $f''(c)=0$: check the first non-zero higher derivative; odd order → no extremum (point of inflection), even order → extremum.

s.q: Absolute extrema on $[a,b]$
s.f: \text{compare } f\ \text{at critical points and at } a,\ b

s.q: Point of inflection
s.f: f''(x)\ \text{changes sign};\ \ \text{concave up if } f''>0,\ \text{down if } f''<0

s.q: Critical points
Global extremum of a cubic on $\mathbb R$
s.f: \text{none (cubic is unbounded)};\ \text{local max/min exist iff } f'=0\ \text{has distinct roots}

s.q: Maximum of product with constraint using derivative
s.f: \text{express in one variable, differentiate, check sign change}

s.q: Distance from a point to a curve minimised
Concavity and point of inflection condition (cubic)
Standard optimisation results
s.f: \text{fixed perimeter}\Rightarrow\text{square has max area};\quad\text{fixed area}\Rightarrow\text{square has min perimeter}
s.n: Max rectangle in a circle of radius $r$: square, area $2r^2$. Max rectangle in an ellipse: $2ab$.

s.q: Cylinder and cone results
s.f: \text{open cylinder, fixed volume, min surface}: h=r;\quad\text{closed cylinder}: h=2r
s.n: Cone of max volume in a sphere of radius $R$: $h=\frac{4R}3$. Cylinder of max volume in a sphere: $h=\frac{2R}{\sqrt3}$. Cone with fixed slant height, max volume: $\tan\theta=\sqrt2$ (semi-vertical angle).

s.q: Shortest distance from a point to a curve
Number of roots via graph
s.f: f(x)=k\ \text{has as many roots as intersections of } y=f(x) \text{ and } y=k
s.n: Use local max/min values: between them → 3 roots for a cubic.

s.q: Cubic with three real roots
s.f: x^3+px+q=0\ \text{has three distinct real roots iff } 4p^3+27q^2<0

Rectangle of max area inscribed in a semicircle
Window / Norman window
s.f: \text{rectangle + semicircle, perimeter } P:\ \text{max area when width}=\frac{2P}{\pi+4}

s.q: Triangle of max area with fixed perimeter / in a circle
Maximum of $f(x)=\frac{x}{\ln x}$ type — use derivative sign table
s.f: \text{for products/quotients, take log first, then differentiate}

s.q: Number of real roots of $f(x)=0$ using extrema
s.f: \text{if } f(\text{local max})\cdot f(\text{local min})<0\ \text{then three real roots (cubic)}

s.q: Rolle-type existence results
s.f: f(a)=f(b)=0\Rightarrow f'(c)+\lambda f(c)=0\ \text{for some } c\ (\text{apply Rolle to } e^{\lambda x}f)

s: If this type comes, solve like this

s.q: If it asks the interval where $f$ is increasing / decreasing
s.n: Factor $f'$, mark zeros and points where $f'$ is undefined (e.g. $x^{2/3}$ at $0$), and read signs. Remember the domain (logs!).

s.q: If it asks the number of real roots of a polynomial/exponential equation
s.f: \text{study } g(x)\ \text{with } g',\ \text{or substitute } t=e^x \text{ and count positive roots}
s.n: Find local max/min values; roots = number of sign changes along the monotonic pieces. For $5x^3-15x-a=0$: three roots iff $a$ lies strictly between the local min and max values.

s.q: If it is a related-rates problem (sphere with coating, cone filling, cube)
s.n: Write the volume/area in ONE variable using the geometry, then differentiate w.r.t. $t$.

s.q: If $g(x)=f(\phi(x))$ with $f''>0$ and it asks where $g$ increases
If it asks $\frac{g(c)}{g'(c)}$ for an inverse function
If it asks where a cubic has local max/min or with given critical points
s.n: Given critical points ⇒ write $f'(x)=k(x-p)(x-q)$ and integrate, or use $f'(p)=0$ equations for the coefficients.

s.q: If it asks absolute max/min on a closed interval
s.f: \text{compare } f \text{ at end points and at critical points inside}
s.n: With $|\ |$ or $[\ ]$: split the interval where the inside changes sign or crosses integers.

s.q: If it is a geometric optimisation (rectangle under a curve, wire into square+circle, cuboid+hemisphere)
s.f: \text{express the target in one variable, set derivative } 0
s.n: Use the constraint to eliminate the second variable. Standard: max area triangle in a circle is equilateral; max rectangle under $y=c-x^2$ gives $x$ from $c=3x^2$.

s.q: If it asks the closest point of a curve to a line
s.f: \text{tangent to the curve parallel to the line: } f'(x)=m

s.q: If it asks the minimum area of triangle formed by a line through $(h,k)$ with the axes
If $f(x)=\max$ of a trig product like $\sin\frac x2\cos^3\frac x2$
If the expression is $\left(\tfrac{a}{x}\right)^{x^2}$ or $x^{1/x}$
If inequalities between functions are asked via monotonicity/convexity
If it asks the number of critical points or extrema of an integral function
